stories.title: The left and right agree on one thing: no data centers
stories.simple_summary: People in different political groups are joining together to stop new AI data centers from being built in their communities. A Florida county just blocked them for a whole year.
stories.why_it_matters: If you live near where an AI data center might be built, this shows your community can say no — but data centers need huge amounts of electricity and water, so this could affect internet services and costs in your area.

stories.title: Amid legal battles, Suno says it will start watermarking songs
stories.simple_summary: Suno, a company that makes music with AI, is adding a watermark to its songs so people can tell they're AI-made. The company is being sued by musicians who say their music was used without permission.
stories.why_it_matters: If you make or sell music, you should know that AI music will soon be marked as AI — but lawsuits over this are still happening, so the rules aren't settled yet.

stories.title: The messy politics behind Google’s big AI shakeup
stories.simple_summary: Google made big changes to how it organizes its AI teams, but there's disagreement behind the scenes about whether these changes are the right move.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to Google employees and investors — nothing you need to act on, though it could affect what new AI tools Google releases.

stories.title: An African vision of artificial intelligence
stories.simple_summary: The Economist is reporting on how African countries are thinking about developing artificial intelligence.
stories.why_it_matters: This is likely about how Africa can build its own AI technology and not just buy it from other countries, but we can't tell from the headline alone what this means for you.

stories.title: Ex-Spotify employees raise $10M to bring the AI behind its recommendations to e-commerce
stories.simple_summary: Former Spotify employees started a new company that uses AI to guess what products you want to buy next, like how Spotify suggests songs. They just raised $10 million to grow it.
stories.why_it_matters: Online shopping websites might soon get better at suggesting products you actually want — similar to how Netflix recommends movies.

stories.title: Exclusive: Mirendil inks $100M+ Google Cloud deal to scale self-improving AI
stories.simple_summary: A company called Mirendil got over $100 million from Google to build AI systems that improve themselves and help scientists work faster.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and scientists — nothing you need to act on right now.

stories.title: AI bots started a religion — humans immediately followed
stories.simple_summary: Some people on the internet created AI chatbots that started acting like a made-up religion, and real people began following it as if it were real.
stories.why_it_matters: This shows that people can get confused about what's real when AI talks to them — be careful about believing everything you read online from AI chatbots or the people who talk to them.

stories.title: Google Maps adds agentic features, including food ordering and hotel bookings
stories.simple_summary: Google Maps is adding features so you can order food and book hotels right inside the app, instead of going to separate websites.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use Google Maps, it's becoming more like a personal assistant that can help you complete tasks, making it more convenient but also tracking more about what you do.

stories.title: Omilia raises $67M to scale its customer support platform
stories.simple_summary: A company called Omilia that helps businesses handle customer phone calls and messages with AI just raised $67 million and has grown its yearly revenue to $60 million.
stories.why_it_matters: If you own a small business, AI customer support tools like this are becoming more affordable and common — you may want to know about them for managing customer calls.

stories.title: Students using AI to cheat will face stricter rules, says Danish government
stories.simple_summary: Denmark's government is making stricter rules for students who use AI to cheat on homework or tests.
stories.why_it_matters: If you have school-age grandchildren, their schools may soon have tougher punishments for using AI to do schoolwork — similar to how plagiarism has always been penalized.

stories.title: OpenAI says Apple’s trade secrets lawsuit is ‘rotten to its core’
stories.simple_summary: OpenAI is fighting Apple's lawsuit that says OpenAI stole Apple's trade secrets. OpenAI says the lawsuit makes no sense and should be thrown out.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly a legal battle between big companies — nothing you need to act on, though the outcome could affect how AI companies can hire and work with employees.

stories.title: Google is expanding its AI empire — and losing the people who built it
stories.simple_summary: Google is hiring more people and expanding its AI business, but experienced workers who built Google's AI are leaving the company.
stories.why_it_matters: This shows that even successful AI companies struggle to keep talented employees happy — mostly interesting to people following the tech industry.
